```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(C50)
library(caret)
```

### Load in Data
```{r}
# Get the train and test data from rds (created in 09_Clean_Data.Rmd, same
# 50/50 split used by the other models).
# We use the un-normalized version: a tree splits on one variable at a time
# (e.g. first_month_streams > 100,000), so rescaling does not change the tree,
# and keeping the original units makes the splits readable.
song_train <- readRDS("rds/song_train.rds")
song_test <- readRDS("rds/song_test.rds")
str(song_train)

# Only ~10% of songs are hits, in both sets
prop.table(table(song_train$hit))
prop.table(table(song_test$hit))
```

### Helper functions
```{r}
# Because only ~10% of songs are hits, predicting "not a hit" every time is
# already ~90% accurate. So, like KNN, we judge every model on kappa.

# turn hit probabilities into 0/1 predictions
to_bin <- function(prob, cutoff = 0.5) {
  factor(ifelse(prob >= cutoff, "1", "0"), levels = c("0", "1"))
}

# one row of metrics for the comparison table at the end
get_metrics <- function(cm) {
  c(accuracy = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
    kappa = unname(cm$overall["Kappa"]),
    sensitivity = unname(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
    specificity = unname(cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
    precision = unname(cm$byClass["Pos Pred Value"]))
}

# 5-fold cross validation on the TRAINING data only. Each improvement below
# is tuned with this, so the test data is never used to pick settings and the
# test results stay an honest estimate.
# Returns the out-of-fold hit probability for every training song.
set.seed(12345)
folds <- createFolds(song_train$hit, k = 5)

cv_probs <- function(...) {
  probs <- numeric(nrow(song_train))
  for (fold in folds) {
    model <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train[-fold, ], ...)
    probs[fold] <- predict(model, song_train[fold, ], type = "prob")[, "1"]
  }
  probs
}

cv_kappa <- function(probs, cutoff = 0.5) {
  confusionMatrix(to_bin(probs, cutoff), song_train$hit,
                  positive = "1")$overall["Kappa"]
}
```

### Baseline Model
```{r}
# Plain C5.0 tree with default settings
set.seed(12345)
dt_base <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train)
dt_base

# which variables the tree actually uses
C5imp(dt_base)
```

```{r}
dt_base_prob <- predict(dt_base, song_test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
cm_dt_base <- confusionMatrix(to_bin(dt_base_prob), song_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_dt_base
```

The baseline tree leans almost entirely on `first_month_streams`, `slow_burner`
and `halflife_days`; the audio features (energy, valence, ...) are barely used.

### Improvement 1: Pruning (tune CF and minCases)
```{r}
# The default tree is allowed to keep splitting down to 2 songs per leaf, which
# risks memorising noise. Two settings control how big the tree gets:
#   minCases - smallest number of songs allowed in a leaf (default 2)
#   CF       - pruning confidence, lower = prune harder (default 0.25)
prune_grid <- expand.grid(CF = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5),
                          minCases = c(2, 5, 10, 25, 50))
prune_grid$cv_kappa <- NA

for (i in 1:nrow(prune_grid)) {
  probs <- cv_probs(control = C5.0Control(CF = prune_grid$CF[i],
                                          minCases = prune_grid$minCases[i]))
  prune_grid$cv_kappa[i] <- cv_kappa(probs)
}
prune_grid[order(-prune_grid$cv_kappa), ]

best_prune <- prune_grid[which.max(prune_grid$cv_kappa), ]
best_control <- C5.0Control(CF = best_prune$CF, minCases = best_prune$minCases)
best_prune
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
dt_pruned <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train, control = best_control)
dt_pruned

dt_pruned_prob <- predict(dt_pruned, song_test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
cm_dt_pruned <- confusionMatrix(to_bin(dt_pruned_prob), song_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_dt_pruned
```

### Improvement 2: Cost matrix (penalise missed hits)
```{r}
# With 90% non-hits the tree is cautious about calling anything a hit. A cost
# matrix tells C5.0 that missing a real hit (false negative) is worse than a
# false alarm. Rows = predicted, columns = actual.
make_costs <- function(fn_cost) {
  matrix(c(0, 1,         # actual 0: predicted 0 is free, predicted 1 costs 1
           fn_cost, 0),  # actual 1: predicted 0 costs fn_cost, predicted 1 is free
         nrow = 2, dimnames = list(predicted = c("0", "1"), actual = c("0", "1")))
}

cost_grid <- data.frame(fn_cost = c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4), cv_kappa = NA)
for (i in 1:nrow(cost_grid)) {
  # (cost-sensitive trees give 0/1 calls, not probabilities, so the CV is
  # written out here instead of using cv_probs)
  pred <- factor(rep("0", nrow(song_train)), levels = c("0", "1"))
  for (fold in folds) {
    model <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train[-fold, ], control = best_control,
                  costs = make_costs(cost_grid$fn_cost[i]))
    pred[fold] <- predict(model, song_train[fold, ])
  }
  cost_grid$cv_kappa[i] <- confusionMatrix(pred, song_train$hit,
                                           positive = "1")$overall["Kappa"]
}
cost_grid

best_fn_cost <- cost_grid$fn_cost[which.max(cost_grid$cv_kappa)]
best_fn_cost
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
dt_cost <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train, control = best_control,
                costs = make_costs(best_fn_cost))

dt_cost_pred <- predict(dt_cost, song_test)
cm_dt_cost <- confusionMatrix(dt_cost_pred, song_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_dt_cost
```

If the best `fn_cost` above is 1, cross validation found that penalising missed
hits did not help, so this version is identical to Improvement 1. Higher costs
catch more hits but add enough false alarms that kappa drops.

### Improvement 3: Boosting (trials)
```{r}
# Instead of one tree, build several in a row, where each new tree focuses on
# the songs the previous ones got wrong, and let them vote.
trial_grid <- data.frame(trials = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40), cv_kappa = NA)
boost_cv <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(trial_grid)) {
  set.seed(12345)
  boost_cv[[i]] <- cv_probs(trials = trial_grid$trials[i], control = best_control)
  trial_grid$cv_kappa[i] <- cv_kappa(boost_cv[[i]])
}
trial_grid

plot(trial_grid$trials, trial_grid$cv_kappa, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Boosting trials", ylab = "Cross-validated kappa",
     main = "Decision Tree Kappa by Boosting Trials")

best_trials <- trial_grid$trials[which.max(trial_grid$cv_kappa)]
best_trials
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
dt_boost <- C5.0(hit ~ ., data = song_train, trials = best_trials,
                 control = best_control)

dt_boost_prob <- predict(dt_boost, song_test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
cm_dt_boost <- confusionMatrix(to_bin(dt_boost_prob), song_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_dt_boost
```

### Improvement 4: Tune the probability cutoff
```{r}
# A 0.5 cutoff is not necessarily the best one when hits are rare. Using the
# cross-validated probabilities from the boosted model, step along the cutoff
# and keep the one with the highest kappa (same idea as the KNN cutoff).
cutoff_grid <- data.frame(cutoff = seq(0.2, 0.7, by = 0.05), cv_kappa = NA)
best_boost_cv <- boost_cv[[which.max(trial_grid$cv_kappa)]]

for (i in 1:nrow(cutoff_grid)) {
  cutoff_grid$cv_kappa[i] <- cv_kappa(best_boost_cv, cutoff_grid$cutoff[i])
}
cutoff_grid

best_cutoff <- cutoff_grid$cutoff[which.max(cutoff_grid$cv_kappa)]
best_cutoff
```

```{r}
cm_dt_cutoff <- confusionMatrix(to_bin(dt_boost_prob, best_cutoff),
                                song_test$hit, positive = "1")
cm_dt_cutoff
```

### Compare all versions
```{r}
# test-set results for every version
dt_compare <- rbind(
  "Baseline" = get_metrics(cm_dt_base),
  "Improvement 1: Pruning" = get_metrics(cm_dt_pruned),
  "Improvement 2: Cost matrix" = get_metrics(cm_dt_cost),
  "Improvement 3: Boosting" = get_metrics(cm_dt_boost),
  "Improvement 4: Boosting + cutoff" = get_metrics(cm_dt_cutoff)
)
round(dt_compare, 4)
```

### Final Model
```{r}
# Final model = pruned + boosted tree with the tuned cutoff (Improvements 1, 3
# and 4). The cost matrix (Improvement 2) is left out because it does the same
# job as the cutoff, and a cost-sensitive tree cannot give the probabilities
# the stacked model needs.
song_dt_predict <- dt_boost_prob
names(song_dt_predict) <- rownames(song_test)
song_dt_bin <- to_bin(song_dt_predict, best_cutoff)
summary(song_dt_bin)

cm_dt <- cm_dt_cutoff
cm_dt
```

### Save to RDS
```{r}
# save probabilities to rds to be used in stacked model
saveRDS(song_dt_predict, "rds/dt_predict.rds")

# save confusion matrix to rds
saveRDS(cm_dt, "rds/cm_dt.rds")
```
